data.gender_notes: Sigismondo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Germanic name Sigismund, meaning 'victory of God'. This name has been popular among European royalty throughout history, including Holy Roman Emperor Sigismund and Hungarian King Sigismund. The name Sigismondo carries the meaning “Victory of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sigismondo usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: זיגיסמונדו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: זיגיסמונדו הוא שם שמקורו בגרמנית ומשמעותו 'זיג' שפירושו נצחון ו'מונדו' שפירושו מגן או מונד. השם נגזר מהשפה הגרמנית ומשמש כסמל לנצחון והגנה. השם מוכר גם בקשר למלכים ואצילים באירופה, ביניהם זיגיסמונד הקדוש, מלך הונגריה וקיסר האימפריה הרומית הקדושה.

in_greek.name: Ζίγισμονδο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ζίγισμονδο προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'ζίγ' που σημαίνει νίκη και 'μούνδο' που σημαίνει προστασία ή ασπίδα. Το όνομα συνδέεται με τη χριστιανική παράδοση και συγκεκριμένα με τον Άγιο Ζίγισμονδο, ο οποίος ήταν βασιλιάς της Ουγγαρίας και αυτοκράτορας της Αγίας Ρωμαϊκής Αυτοκρατορίας.

in_latin.name: Sigismondo
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Sigismondo originates from the Germanic languages, derived from 'sieg' meaning victory and 'mund' meaning protector or guardian. The name gained prominence through its association with Sigismund, a saint and king of Hungary who later became Holy Roman Emperor. The name symbolizes strength, victory, and protection, reflecting its bearer as a champion of faith and a guardian of the faithful.

in_english.name: Sigismondo
in_english.meaning: Sigismondo means victorious protector or strong guardian
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sigismondo is of Germanic origin, derived from 'sieg' meaning victory and 'mund' meaning protector. It is associated with Saint Sigismund, a 5th-century king of Burgundy and later a saint venerated in the Roman Catholic Church. The name signifies a champion of faith, a victorious guardian, and a strong protector. Historically, it was borne by several European monarchs, including a king of Hungary and a Holy Roman Emperor, emphasizing its connection to royalty and spiritual leadership.
